verdict.rationale: LiteLLM lets users configure rules that act automatically on specific gateway events. A failed call after num_retries triggers fallback to another model group, content-policy violations can trigger content_policy_fallbacks, and proxy logging can invoke custom callbacks (custom code and API endpoints) on requests and exceptions. These are narrow, reliability- and logging-specific triggers rather than a general rule engine. Missing for 10: a general user-defined event→action rules engine, arbitrary event types and action targets beyond fallback and logging callbacks, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: If a call fails after num_retries, LiteLLM falls back to another model group, so a failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup.
